entries.meaning: To give someone what they need or ask for. ---
examples: The school provides free lunch to every student.
They provided blankets after the storm.
We are providing transportation for the out-of-town guests.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (provide lunch), intransitive (provide for a family)
entries.contrast: Two patterns, both with a preposition: provide someone with something, or provide something for someone. Never provide me a pen.

entries.meaning: To give money, goods, or blood to a charity or other organization. ---
examples: Many families donate clothes in December.
He donated his old laptop to the library.
They have been donating blood twice a year since college.

entries.meaning: Contribute has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Everyone at work contributes five dollars a month.
She contributed two hundred dollars to the relief fund.
He has contributed three articles to the magazine this year.
Smoking contributes to heart disease.
Poor lighting contributed to the accident.
Several factors have contributed to the delay.

senses.head: To give money, effort, or ideas as your part of something shared
examples: Everyone at work contributes five dollars a month.
She contributed two hundred dollars to the relief fund.
He has contributed three articles to the magazine this year.

senses.head: To be one of the causes of something
examples: Smoking contributes to heart disease.
Poor lighting contributed to the accident.
Several factors have contributed to the delay.

entries.русский: вносить вклад, жертвовать, внести; способствовать, быть одной из причин
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (contribute an article), intransitive (everyone contributed)
entries.contrast: Stress is on the second syllable — kuhn-TRIB-yoot, not CON-tri-byoot — and the money goes to something: contribute to a fund.

entries.meaning: To pass something to someone using your hands. ---
examples: Please hand me the scissors.
He handed the keys to his brother without a word.
The waiter is handing each guest a menu.
entries.phrasal verbs: hand down · hand down · hand in · hand it to · hand off · hand out · hand over

entries.meaning: Share has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The two boys share a bedroom.
She shared her notes with the whole class.
They have been sharing a car since March.
Thanks for sharing your story with us.
She shared the news with her family first.
He never shares what he is feeling.

senses.head: To have or use something together with someone else, or to give part of it away
examples: The two boys share a bedroom.
She shared her notes with the whole class.
They have been sharing a car since March.

senses.head: To tell someone about your thoughts, feelings, or news
examples: Thanks for sharing your story with us.
She shared the news with her family first.
He never shares what he is feeling.

entries.русский: делить, делиться, поделиться; делиться (мыслями, новостями), поделиться; рассказывать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (share a room), intransitive (children learn to share)
entries.contrast: You share something with a person: share the pizza with me, not share me the pizza.

entries.meaning: To give out something official, such as a document, a permit, or a statement. ---
examples: The office issues parking permits on Mondays.
The court issued a warrant that same afternoon.
They are issuing refunds to everyone who paid the old rate.

entries.meaning: Grant has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The city grants permits to only ten vendors a year.
The judge granted the request without comment.
He was granted citizenship last spring.
I'll grant you that the price is high.
She granted the point and moved on.
Granted, the weather could have been better.

senses.head: To give someone something officially, especially permission or a right
examples: The city grants permits to only ten vendors a year.
The judge granted the request without comment.
He was granted citizenship last spring.

senses.head: To admit that something is true, even when it does not change your opinion
examples: I'll grant you that the price is high.
She granted the point and moved on.
Granted, the weather could have been better.

entries.русский: предоставлять, предоставить, даровать; признавать, признать; допускать, согласиться
entries.contrast: American /æ/: GRANT rhymes with ant, not with the British /ɑː/.

entries.meaning: To give someone a prize, a sum of money, or a contract as an official decision. ---
examples: They award one full scholarship a year.
The jury awarded her two million dollars.
He has been awarded three patents since 2019.

entries.meaning: To give each person or purpose a fixed amount or share. ---
examples: They allot each speaker ten minutes.
The school allotted us two parking spaces.
Only an hour was allotted for questions.
entries.contrast: Stress on the last syllable doubles the t: allotted, allotting.

entries.meaning: To give out measured amounts of something, especially medicine or supplies. ---
examples: The machine dispenses coffee, tea, and hot chocolate.
The nurse dispensed the medication herself.
They are dispensing free masks at the entrance.

entries.meaning: Submit has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You submit the application online.
She submitted her résumé on Tuesday.
He has submitted the same essay twice.
He refused to submit to the guards.
The city finally submitted after a long siege.
Having submitted to a search, she was waved through.

senses.head: To hand in a document or piece of work for someone to consider
examples: You submit the application online.
She submitted her résumé on Tuesday.
He has submitted the same essay twice.

senses.head: To stop resisting and accept someone else's power or authority
examples: He refused to submit to the guards.
The city finally submitted after a long siege.
Having submitted to a search, she was waved through.

entries.русский: подавать, представлять, подать; подчиняться, подчиниться; покоряться, уступать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (submit a form), intransitive (he refused to submit)
entries.contrast: Stress on the last syllable doubles the t: submitted, submitting.

entries.meaning: To give something up to someone else, especially because you are forced to. ---
examples: You must surrender your license at the front desk.
The driver surrendered his keys without arguing.
They are surrendering the property to the bank next month.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (surrender your passport), intransitive (the soldiers surrendered)

entries.meaning: Sacrifice has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Parents often sacrifice their own plans for their kids.
She sacrificed a whole weekend to finish the project.
He has sacrificed a lot for that career.
Some cultures still sacrifice an animal at harvest time.
The priests sacrificed a goat each spring.
The lamb was sacrificed on the altar.

senses.head: To give up something you value in order to get or protect something else
examples: Parents often sacrifice their own plans for their kids.
She sacrificed a whole weekend to finish the project.
He has sacrificed a lot for that career.

senses.head: To kill an animal or a person as an offering to a god
examples: Some cultures still sacrifice an animal at harvest time.
The priests sacrificed a goat each spring.
The lamb was sacrificed on the altar.

entries.русский: жертвовать, пожертвовать; приносить в жертву, принести в жертву
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (sacrifice a weekend), intransitive (parents sacrifice)
entries.contrast: The ending is /faɪs/ with an s sound — SAK-ruh-fyss, not "-fyze".

entries.meaning: To give your time, money, or effort entirely to one thing. ---
examples: They devote every Sunday to family.
He devoted thirty years to that school.
She is devoting her savings to the trip.
entries.contrast: Devote something to something: devoted his life to teaching.

entries.meaning: To set something aside for one purpose, or to name a work in someone's honor. ---
examples: They dedicate one small room to storage.
The author dedicated the book to her mother.
A bench has been dedicated to him in the park.

entries.meaning: To give something or someone into another person's care, trusting them with it. ---
examples: I would entrust him with anything.
She entrusted the money to her sister.
The files were entrusted to a lawyer downtown.
entries.contrast: Two patterns: entrust someone with something, or entrust something to someone.

entries.meaning: Confer has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The university confers degrees in May.
The title was conferred on him in 1998.
The judges are conferring before they announce a winner.
Let me confer with my partner and call you back.
The referees conferred for a full minute.
The judges have been conferring since lunch.

senses.head: To grant someone an honor, a title, or a right formally
examples: The university confers degrees in May.
The title was conferred on him in 1998.
The judges are conferring before they announce a winner.

senses.head: To talk something over with other people before deciding
examples: Let me confer with my partner and call you back.
The referees conferred for a full minute.
The judges have been conferring since lunch.

entries.русский: присваивать, присвоить, даровать; совещаться, посовещаться; советоваться, обсуждать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (confer a degree), intransitive (confer with a colleague)
entries.contrast: Stress on the last syllable doubles the r: conferred, conferring.

entries.meaning: To give something to someone as a present, with no payment expected. ---
examples: Her parents gift the kids books every birthday.
A neighbor gifted us a set of kitchen chairs.
The land was gifted to the town in 1970.

entries.meaning: Treat has 4 distinct senses.
examples: Let me treat you to lunch.
Her uncle treated everyone to ice cream.
He is treating the whole team to dinner tonight.
They treat their employees well.
He treated her like a stranger.
I don't like being treated as a child.
Doctors treat the infection with antibiotics.
Paramedics treated her at the scene.
He is being treated for a broken wrist.
We treat the deck every other spring.
They treated the water before pumping it into town.
The lumber has been treated to resist rot.

senses.head: To pay for something enjoyable for someone else as a gift
examples: Let me treat you to lunch.
Her uncle treated everyone to ice cream.
He is treating the whole team to dinner tonight.

senses.head: To behave toward someone or something in a particular way
examples: They treat their employees well.
He treated her like a stranger.
I don't like being treated as a child.

senses.head: To give medical care to a person or an illness
examples: Doctors treat the infection with antibiotics.
Paramedics treated her at the scene.
He is being treated for a broken wrist.

senses.head: To put a chemical on something in order to protect it or change it
examples: We treat the deck every other spring.
They treated the water before pumping it into town.
The lumber has been treated to resist rot.

entries.русский: угощать, угостить; обращаться, относиться (к кому-л.); лечить, вылечить; оказывать помощь; обрабатывать, обработать (составом)
entries.contrast: Treat someone to something: treated us to coffee.

entries.meaning: Tip has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Americans usually tip about twenty percent.
We tipped the driver ten dollars.
She is tipping in cash tonight.
Don't tip your chair back like that.
He tipped the bucket and poured the water into the sink.
The canoe was tipping dangerously in the wind.

senses.head: To give a server, driver, or other worker extra money for their service
examples: Americans usually tip about twenty percent.
We tipped the driver ten dollars.
She is tipping in cash tonight.

senses.head: To lean to one side or fall over, or to make something do that
examples: Don't tip your chair back like that.
He tipped the bucket and poured the water into the sink.
The canoe was tipping dangerously in the wind.

entries.русский: давать чаевые, дать на чай; наклонять, наклонить; опрокидывать, опрокинуть
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (tip the driver), intransitive (Americans tip well)
entries.contrast: Short vowel plus one consonant doubles it: tipped, tipping.

entries.meaning: To give someone something in return for good work or good behavior. ---
examples: Good schools reward effort, not just talent.
The company rewarded her with a bonus.
Honest work is rarely rewarded that quickly.

entries.meaning: Compensate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The airline will compensate passengers for the delay.
They compensated him for the damage to his fence.
Nothing is compensating us for the lost weekend.
A good lens can compensate for poor light.
She compensated for a thin résumé with a strong interview.
The engine runs rough, and the computer is constantly compensating for it.

senses.head: To pay someone money to make up for a loss, injury, or inconvenience
examples: The airline will compensate passengers for the delay.
They compensated him for the damage to his fence.
Nothing is compensating us for the lost weekend.

senses.head: To balance out a weakness or a loss by doing something else
examples: A good lens can compensate for poor light.
She compensated for a thin résumé with a strong interview.
The engine runs rough, and the computer is constantly compensating for it.

entries.русский: возмещать, компенсировать, возместить; компенсировать, восполнять (недостаток), возмещать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (compensate the workers), intransitive (compensate for a loss)

entries.meaning: To pay someone back money they have already spent. ---
examples: The company reimburses travel costs within reason.
They reimbursed me two weeks after I sent the receipts.
Her tuition is being reimbursed by her employer.

entries.meaning: To give a customer back the money they paid. ---
examples: They refund the deposit at checkout.
The store refunded the full price without asking questions.
My ticket has not been refunded yet.
entries.contrast: The verb is ri-FUND /rɪˈfʌnd/; the noun a refund is REE-fund /ˈriːfʌnd/.

entries.meaning: To pass something on to someone, especially a message, a feeling, or property. ---
examples: Please convey my thanks to your parents.
The letter conveyed the news as gently as possible.
Nothing in his voice was conveying anger.
entries.contrast: A vowel before the y keeps it: conveys, conveyed — not convies, convied.

entries.meaning: Fetch has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Would you fetch a chair from the kitchen?
The dog fetched the stick every single time.
She is fetching water from the pump out back.
The painting could fetch two million dollars.
His old guitar fetched far more than he expected.
Beach houses here have fetched record prices this year.

senses.head: To go somewhere, pick something up, and bring it back
examples: Would you fetch a chair from the kitchen?
The dog fetched the stick every single time.
She is fetching water from the pump out back.

senses.head: To be sold for a particular price
examples: The painting could fetch two million dollars.
His old guitar fetched far more than he expected.
Beach houses here have fetched record prices this year.

entries.русский: приносить, принести, сходить за; выручать (сумму), уходить за (цену), принести (на торгах)

entries.meaning: To give one thing and receive another in its place. ---
examples: You can exchange it for a larger size.
They exchanged phone numbers at the party.
We have been exchanging letters for almost ten years.
entries.contrast: Exchange one thing for another: exchanged the shirt for a jacket.

entries.meaning: To trade one thing for another, usually informally. ---
examples: Let's swap seats — I can't see the board.
They swapped shifts without telling the manager.
The kids are swapping stickers again.
entries.contrast: Short vowel plus one consonant doubles it: swapped, swapping.

entries.meaning: Trade has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I'll trade you my sandwich for your apple.
He traded his bike for an old guitar.
They are trading baseball cards at recess.
He trades bonds for a hedge fund.
The stock traded below ten dollars all week.
Oil has been trading near record highs.

senses.head: To give something to someone and get something of theirs in return
examples: I'll trade you my sandwich for your apple.
He traded his bike for an old guitar.
They are trading baseball cards at recess.

senses.head: To buy and sell stocks, currency, or commodities on a market
examples: He trades bonds for a hedge fund.
The stock traded below ten dollars all week.
Oil has been trading near record highs.

entries.русский: обменивать, менять, торговать; торговать (на бирже); котироваться
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (trade cards), intransitive (the store trades in antiques)
entries.phrasal verbs: trade in · trade on · trade up

entries.meaning: To put money into a bank account, or to place something somewhere for safekeeping. ---
examples: I deposit my paycheck every other Friday.
She deposited the check from her phone.
The refund has already been deposited.
entries.contrast: Stress is on the middle syllable, so nothing doubles: deposited, depositing.

entries.meaning: To send on a letter, message, or email to someone else. ---
examples: Please forward the email to my manager.
He forwarded the message to the whole team by mistake.
Her mail is being forwarded to the new address.

entries.meaning: Post has 4 distinct senses.
examples: They post the schedule every Sunday night.
She posted the photos about an hour ago.
He has been posting about the sale all week.
The Army posted him to Germany for three years.
They post a guard at the gate every night.
She has been posted overseas twice since 2019.
The airline posted a record profit last quarter.
Analysts expect the company to post another loss.
The chain has posted three straight quarters of growth.
His brother posted bail the same night.
She could not afford to post a $10,000 bond.
Bail was posted by an anonymous donor.

senses.head: To put a notice, message, or picture where others can see it, especially online
examples: They post the schedule every Sunday night.
She posted the photos about an hour ago.
He has been posting about the sale all week.

senses.head: To send someone to a particular place to work or to stand guard
body: (назначать (на должность, в место службы), направлять; выставлять (охрану))
examples: The Army posted him to Germany for three years.
They post a guard at the gate every night.
She has been posted overseas twice since 2019.

senses.head: To officially announce a financial result such as a profit or a loss
examples: The airline posted a record profit last quarter.
Analysts expect the company to post another loss.
The chain has posted three straight quarters of growth.

senses.head: To pay money to a court so that an accused person can stay out of jail until the trial
examples: His brother posted bail the same night.
She could not afford to post a $10,000 bond.
Bail was posted by an anonymous donor.

entries.русский: публиковать, размещать, выложить; назначать (на должность, в место службы), направлять; выставлять (охрану); объявлять (финансовые результаты), сообщать; показать (прибыль, убыток); вносить залог, внести залог
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (post a photo), intransitive (he posts every day)

entries.meaning: Divide has 3 distinct senses.
examples: We always divide the check evenly.
She divided the cake into eight pieces.
The money is being divided among the four cousins.
Divide twelve by four and you get three.
She divided the bill by the number of guests.
Dividing by zero is not allowed.
The issue divides the whole country.
The proposal divided the board for months.
It is a question that has divided families.

senses.head: To separate something into parts and give each part to someone
examples: We always divide the check evenly.
She divided the cake into eight pieces.
The money is being divided among the four cousins.

senses.head: To find how many times one number goes into another
examples: Divide twelve by four and you get three.
She divided the bill by the number of guests.
Dividing by zero is not allowed.

senses.head: To make people disagree strongly with one another
examples: The issue divides the whole country.
The proposal divided the board for months.
It is a question that has divided families.

entries.русский: делить, разделить, распределять; делить, разделить (в арифметике); разделять, раскалывать (общество, группу)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (divide the cake), intransitive (the road divides here)
entries.contrast: Divide something between two people, among three or more.

entries.meaning: To give out something scarce in small fixed amounts. ---
examples: We ration the water on long hikes.
The government rationed sugar during the war.
They are rationing the last of the fuel.
entries.contrast: The n never doubles: rationed, rationing.

entries.meaning: Guarantee has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We guarantee delivery in two business days.
The shop guaranteed the repair for a full year.
Nothing is guaranteed in this business.
Her father guaranteed the lease.
The government guarantees deposits up to a set amount.
The loan is guaranteed by the state.

senses.head: To promise that something will happen or that a product will work
examples: We guarantee delivery in two business days.
The shop guaranteed the repair for a full year.
Nothing is guaranteed in this business.

senses.head: To agree to be responsible for someone else's debt if they fail to pay it
examples: Her father guaranteed the lease.
The government guarantees deposits up to a set amount.
The loan is guaranteed by the state.

entries.русский: гарантировать, ручаться, поручиться; выступать поручителем, поручиться; гарантировать (заём)
entries.contrast: Silent u after the g, and the -ee just takes a d: guaranteed, but guaranteeing keeps all three es.

entries.meaning: Volunteer has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Several parents volunteer at the book fair.
He volunteered to drive everyone home.
She has been volunteering at the animal shelter since June.
Don't volunteer anything the officer hasn't asked about.
He volunteered that he had been in the building that night.
Nobody has volunteered an explanation yet.

senses.head: To offer your time or help freely, without being asked or paid
examples: Several parents volunteer at the book fair.
He volunteered to drive everyone home.
She has been volunteering at the animal shelter since June.

senses.head: To give information that nobody has asked you for
examples: Don't volunteer anything the officer hasn't asked about.
He volunteered that he had been in the building that night.
Nobody has volunteered an explanation yet.

entries.русский: вызваться, предлагать помощь, работать добровольцем; сообщать по собственной инициативе, вызваться сказать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (volunteer your time), intransitive (she volunteers at the shelter)

entries.meaning: Credit has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They credit the refund to your card automatically.
The store credited my account the next day.
Twenty dollars has been credited to your balance.
She credits her mother with teaching her to cook.
He credited the win to his teammates.
Fleming is credited with discovering penicillin.

senses.head: To add money to someone's account
examples: They credit the refund to your card automatically.
The store credited my account the next day.
Twenty dollars has been credited to your balance.

senses.head: To say publicly that someone is responsible for something good
examples: She credits her mother with teaching her to cook.
He credited the win to his teammates.
Fleming is credited with discovering penicillin.

entries.русский: зачислять, зачислить, приписывать; приписывать (заслугу), отдавать должное
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t never doubles: credited, crediting.

entries.meaning: To supply the money for something large, often as a loan. ---
examples: Banks finance most projects of this size.
They financed the car over five years.
The building is being financed by the state.

entries.meaning: Sponsor has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Local businesses sponsor the team every season.
A bank sponsored the concert last summer.
They are sponsoring three students this year.
She plans to sponsor legislation on clean water.
Two senators sponsored the bill last spring.
The measure is sponsored by lawmakers from both parties.
His employer agreed to sponsor his visa.
She sponsored her mother for a green card.
He was sponsored by an uncle who already lived in Chicago.

senses.head: To pay for an event, a team, or a person, usually in return for publicity
examples: Local businesses sponsor the team every season.
A bank sponsored the concert last summer.
They are sponsoring three students this year.

senses.head: To formally put a bill or a proposal forward in a legislature
examples: She plans to sponsor legislation on clean water.
Two senators sponsored the bill last spring.
The measure is sponsored by lawmakers from both parties.

senses.head: To take formal responsibility for someone so that they can enter a country or join a group
examples: His employer agreed to sponsor his visa.
She sponsored her mother for a green card.
He was sponsored by an uncle who already lived in Chicago.

entries.русский: спонсировать, финансировать, поддерживать; вносить, внести (законопроект); быть автором законопроекта; выступать поручителем, поручиться; оформлять спонсорство (визу, грин-карту)

entries.meaning: To let someone have or do something. ---
examples: They allow dogs on the patio.
The teacher allowed us an extra day.
Photography is not allowed inside the museum.
entries.contrast: Allowed sounds exactly like aloud: they allowed him to speak, but read it aloud.

entries.meaning: To let something or someone go, or to make something available to the public. ---
examples: They release the results on Friday.
The hospital released him after two days.
The album is being released in March.
entries.contrast: Written -ase but pronounced -eess /iːs/, not -eez.

entries.meaning: To choose not to demand a fee, a rule, or a right you are entitled to. ---
examples: They will waive the application fee for students.
The bank waived the charge after I called.
Late fees are being waived this month.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like wave, but the spellings split: you waive a fee and wave your hand.

entries.meaning: To lose or give up something as a penalty for breaking a rule or agreement. ---
examples: You forfeit the deposit if you cancel late.
They forfeited the game when only four players showed up.
He has forfeited his right to appeal.
entries.contrast: The ei is only /ɪ/: FAWR-fit, not "for-FEET".

entries.meaning: Receive has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We receive about fifty applications a week.
She received the package yesterday.
He has received no answer at all.
How will voters receive the plan?
The audience received the speech warmly.
Her first novel was well received by critics.

senses.head: To get something that is sent or given to you
examples: We receive about fifty applications a week.
She received the package yesterday.
He has received no answer at all.

senses.head: To react to something or someone in a particular way
examples: How will voters receive the plan?
The audience received the speech warmly.
Her first novel was well received by critics.

entries.русский: получать, получить; принимать, воспринимать, встречать (о публике, критике)
entries.contrast: i before e except after c: receive, not recieve.

entries.meaning: To get something, especially by effort or through an official process. ---
examples: You obtain the form at the front desk.
They obtained a copy of the contract.
The permit was obtained in a single afternoon.

entries.meaning: To get something useful, or to increase in amount. ---
examples: Members gain access to the entire library.
He gained fifteen pounds over the winter.
She is gaining confidence every week.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (gain access), intransitive (the stock gained today)

entries.meaning: To reach or achieve something you have worked toward. ---
examples: Few runners ever attain that kind of speed.
She attained the rank of captain at thirty.
The goal has not been attained yet.

entries.meaning: To gather things together, or to obtain money that is owed. ---
examples: He collects old road maps.
The driver collected the fares at the door.
They are collecting donations in the lobby.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (collect the fares), intransitive (water collects in the basement)

entries.meaning: Gather has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Squirrels gather nuts all through the fall.
A crowd gathered outside the courthouse.
We are gathering signatures for the petition.
I gather you two have already met.
From her voice he gathered that the news was bad.
We had gathered as much from her email.

senses.head: To bring things or people together into one place
examples: Squirrels gather nuts all through the fall.
A crowd gathered outside the courthouse.
We are gathering signatures for the petition.

senses.head: To understand or conclude something from what you have seen or heard
examples: I gather you two have already met.
From her voice he gathered that the news was bad.
We had gathered as much from her email.

entries.русский: собирать, собираться, собрать; понимать, заключать, сделать вывод
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (gather the papers), intransitive (a crowd gathered)

entries.meaning: To collect a very large amount of something over time. ---
examples: Few people amass that kind of wealth honestly.
He amassed a collection of ten thousand records.
They have amassed enough evidence to file charges.

entries.meaning: To gather up more and more of something over a period of time. ---
examples: Dust accumulates fast in this room.
She accumulated six weeks of unused vacation.
Snow has been accumulating since midnight.
entries.contrast: Double c, single m: accumulate.

entries.meaning: To collect and hide away a large supply of something, often more than you need. ---
examples: Some shoppers hoard bottled water before a storm.
He hoarded newspapers for forty years.
People were hoarding canned food that spring.
entries.contrast: Sounds like horde (a horde of tourists), but hoard is the verb for storing things away.

entries.meaning: Reserve has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They reserve the front row for family.
I reserved a table for seven o'clock.
That whole section is reserved.
Reserve a cup of the pasta water before you drain it.
The company reserves the right to cancel the order.
I'm reserving judgment until I hear both sides.

senses.head: To arrange for something to be kept for you to use later
examples: They reserve the front row for family.
I reserved a table for seven o'clock.
That whole section is reserved.

senses.head: To hold something back for a special purpose or for later
examples: Reserve a cup of the pasta water before you drain it.
The company reserves the right to cancel the order.
I'm reserving judgment until I hear both sides.

entries.русский: резервировать, бронировать, забронировать; оставлять, приберегать; сохранять за собой (право)

entries.meaning: To receive money, property, or traits from someone who has died or come before you. ---
examples: The children inherit everything equally.
She inherited the farm from her grandfather.
He has inherited his father's temper.
entries.contrast: Stress is in the middle, so nothing doubles: inherited, inheriting.

entries.meaning: To gather a crop when it is ripe. ---
examples: They harvest the corn in late September.
We harvested four bushels of apples in one afternoon.
The wheat is being harvested right now.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (harvest the corn), intransitive (they harvest in October)

entries.meaning: Reap has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Investors reap the profits, not the workers.
She reaped the benefits of all those early mornings.
They are still reaping rewards from that one decision.
In August the farmers reap the wheat.
They reaped the last field just before the storm.
The barley had already been reaped by the time we arrived.

senses.head: To receive the results of something you did earlier, good or bad
examples: Investors reap the profits, not the workers.
She reaped the benefits of all those early mornings.
They are still reaping rewards from that one decision.

senses.head: To cut and gather a crop from a field
examples: In August the farmers reap the wheat.
They reaped the last field just before the storm.
The barley had already been reaped by the time we arrived.

entries.русский: пожинать, получать, пожать; жать, сжать; убирать, собирать (урожай)

entries.meaning: To take something quickly and by force, or to take it by legal authority. ---
examples: Customs officers sometimes seize packages like this.
Police seized the car as evidence.
The property is being seized by the bank.
entries.contrast: An exception to "i before e": seize, not sieze.

entries.meaning: To catch and hold a person, an animal, or a moment. ---
examples: These traps capture the mice alive.
The photo captured the whole street at sunrise.
Two of them were captured near the border.

entries.meaning: Grab has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Grab a coat — it's colder than it looks.
He grabbed my arm before I slipped.
She is grabbing coffee on the way in.
Let's grab a coffee before the meeting.
We grabbed a quick lunch at the airport.
I'm grabbing a seat near the front.
The first chapter really grabs you.
The movie never grabbed me.
Headlines are written to grab your attention.

senses.head: To take hold of something quickly and roughly
examples: Grab a coat — it's colder than it looks.
He grabbed my arm before I slipped.
She is grabbing coffee on the way in.

senses.head: To get or take something quickly and without fuss (informal)
examples: Let's grab a coffee before the meeting.
We grabbed a quick lunch at the airport.
I'm grabbing a seat near the front.

senses.head: To catch and hold someone's interest
examples: The first chapter really grabs you.
The movie never grabbed me.
Headlines are written to grab your attention.

entries.русский: хватать, схватить; быстро взять, перехватить; перекусить; захватывать, увлекать, зацепить
entries.contrast: Short vowel plus one consonant doubles it: grabbed, grabbing.

entries.meaning: To take something suddenly and rudely out of someone's hands. ---
examples: Gulls will snatch food right out of your hand.
Someone snatched her purse on the platform.
The dog is snatching bread off the counter again.

entries.meaning: To take someone's property away officially, as a punishment or for safety. ---
examples: Teachers here confiscate phones during tests.
The guard confiscated his lighter at the gate.
Anything sharp is confiscated at security.

entries.meaning: To get something back from the place where it was left or stored. ---
examples: The app retrieves your old messages.
He retrieved the ball from the neighbor's roof.
She is retrieving her coat from the closet.
entries.contrast: ie, not ei — retrieve, even though receive goes the other way.

entries.meaning: Recover has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Divers sometimes recover things from the bottom of the lake.
Police recovered the stolen bikes two blocks away.
Two of the paintings have been recovered.
It takes about a month to recover from this surgery.
He recovered quickly and was back at work in a week.
The economy has never fully recovered from the shutdown.

senses.head: To get back something that was lost, stolen, or spent
examples: Divers sometimes recover things from the bottom of the lake.
Police recovered the stolen bikes two blocks away.
Two of the paintings have been recovered.

senses.head: To get well again after an illness, or to return to a normal condition after trouble
examples: It takes about a month to recover from this surgery.
He recovered quickly and was back at work in a week.
The economy has never fully recovered from the shutdown.

entries.русский: возвращать, находить, вернуть; выздоравливать, поправляться; восстанавливаться, прийти в себя
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (recover the bikes), intransitive (he recovered slowly)

entries.meaning: Reclaim has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You can reclaim the tax at the airport.
She reclaimed the land after a ten-year fight.
The city is reclaiming the old rail yard.
The city wants to reclaim the old rail yard for housing.
The Dutch reclaimed much of their farmland from the sea.
The floors are made of reclaimed barn wood.

senses.head: To get back something that was taken from you or given up
examples: You can reclaim the tax at the airport.
She reclaimed the land after a ten-year fight.
The city is reclaiming the old rail yard.

senses.head: To make land or material usable again, by draining it or by saving it from waste
examples: The city wants to reclaim the old rail yard for housing.
The Dutch reclaimed much of their farmland from the sea.
The floors are made of reclaimed barn wood.

entries.русский: возвращать себе, истребовать, вернуть; осваивать, отвоёвывать (землю); восстанавливать для повторного использования

entries.meaning: To take a child or an animal into your family permanently, or to take up an idea as your own. ---
examples: Many families adopt through this agency.
They adopted a dog from the county shelter.
She was adopted as a baby.
entries.contrast: Not adapt: you adopt a child, but you adapt to the cold. Nothing doubles: adopted, adopting.

entries.meaning: To hug someone, or to accept an idea eagerly. ---
examples: Younger shoppers embrace the new payment app.
He embraced his brother at the gate.
The idea has been embraced by both parties.

entries.meaning: To put money in your pocket, especially money you should not keep. ---
examples: Middlemen pocket most of the difference.
He pocketed the change without counting it.
She is pocketing half the profit.
entries.contrast: Stress is on the first syllable, so the t never doubles: pocketed, pocketing.

entries.meaning: To take something for a while and give it back later. ---
examples: Students can borrow six books at a time.
I borrowed his car for the weekend.
She has been borrowing money from her sister for months.
entries.contrast: You borrow from someone; they lend to you. Russian одолжить covers both directions, English does not.

entries.meaning: To rent property or equipment under a long written contract. ---
examples: Most drivers here lease their cars.
The company leased two floors downtown.
The land is being leased to a solar farm.
entries.русский: арендовать, сдавать в аренду, взять в аренду
entries.contrast: Ends in /s/, not /z/ — LEESS, rhyming with piece.

entries.meaning: To let someone use your money or property for a while. ---
examples: Neighbors loan each other tools all the time.
He loaned me two hundred dollars until payday.
The painting is loaned to the museum every fall.
entries.contrast: Americans use loan as a verb where the British prefer lend. It sounds like lone.

entries.meaning: Charge has 4 distinct senses.
examples: They charge five dollars for parking.
The plumber charged us double on a Sunday.
You are being charged a monthly fee.
Police charged him with fraud.
Prosecutors will charge both drivers.
She has been charged with two counts of theft.
Charge your phone before the flight.
The battery charges in about an hour.
I left the laptop charging overnight.
The bull charged the fence.
Fans charged onto the field after the final whistle.
He came charging into the room without knocking.

senses.head: To ask someone for a particular amount of money for goods or a service
examples: They charge five dollars for parking.
The plumber charged us double on a Sunday.
You are being charged a monthly fee.

senses.head: To accuse someone formally of a crime
examples: Police charged him with fraud.
Prosecutors will charge both drivers.
She has been charged with two counts of theft.

senses.head: To put electricity into a battery
examples: Charge your phone before the flight.
The battery charges in about an hour.
I left the laptop charging overnight.

senses.head: To rush forward in attack
examples: The bull charged the fence.
Fans charged onto the field after the final whistle.
He came charging into the room without knocking.

entries.русский: брать плату, взимать, назначать цену; обвинять, предъявить обвинение; заряжать, зарядить; атаковать, бросаться в атаку; кидаться
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (charge a fee), intransitive (they charge by the hour)
entries.contrast: Charge someone for something, and charge it to a card.
entries.phrasal verbs: charge up · charge with, charge for

entries.meaning: Owe has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I owe my sister forty dollars.
He owed the bank more than he made in a year.
They still have not paid what is owed.
I owe you an apology.
She owes her whole career to that teacher.
We owed them a favor, so we said yes.

senses.head: To have to pay someone money you have not paid yet
examples: I owe my sister forty dollars.
He owed the bank more than he made in a year.
They still have not paid what is owed.

senses.head: To feel that you should thank or repay someone for what they did
examples: I owe you an apology.
She owes her whole career to that teacher.
We owed them a favor, so we said yes.

entries.русский: быть должным, задолжать; быть обязанным (кому-л. чем-л.)
entries.contrast: The w is silent — owe is just /oʊ/, like oh. Add -d for owed, but drop the e for owing.

entries.meaning: To take away from someone something they need or are entitled to. ---
examples: Long shifts deprive nurses of sleep.
The new rule deprived him of a hearing.
They were deprived of clean water for a week.
entries.contrast: Deprive someone of something — the of is not optional.

entries.meaning: Rob has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They rob the same stretch of highway every winter.
Two men robbed the store right at closing.
He has been robbed twice this year.
Don't let fear rob you of this chance.
A knee injury robbed him of his best years.
The players felt robbed of a fair result.

senses.head: To take money or property from a person or place by force or threat
examples: They rob the same stretch of highway every winter.
Two men robbed the store right at closing.
He has been robbed twice this year.

senses.head: To take away from someone something they need or deserve
examples: Don't let fear rob you of this chance.
A knee injury robbed him of his best years.
The players felt robbed of a fair result.

entries.contrast: Short vowel plus one consonant doubles it: robbed, robbing. You rob a person or a bank, but you steal a thing.

entries.meaning: To take an amount away from a total, especially from a payment. ---
examples: They deduct taxes from every paycheck.
The hotel deducted the deposit from the bill.
Union dues are deducted automatically.

entries.meaning: Save has 4 distinct senses.
examples: We save about three hundred dollars a month.
She saved for two years to buy it.
They have been saving every coupon in a drawer.
Seat belts save thousands of lives a year.
A neighbor saved the dog from the flooded yard.
He was saved by a passing fishing boat.
Save the file before you close the laptop.
I saved the photos to a flash drive.
The document had not been saved, and an hour of work was gone.
Taking the express will save you an hour.
One phone call saved us a trip downtown.
You could have saved yourself a lot of trouble by asking first.

senses.head: To keep money or things instead of spending or using them
examples: We save about three hundred dollars a month.
She saved for two years to buy it.
They have been saving every coupon in a drawer.

senses.head: To take someone or something out of danger
examples: Seat belts save thousands of lives a year.
A neighbor saved the dog from the flooded yard.
He was saved by a passing fishing boat.

senses.head: To store a computer file so that you can use it later
examples: Save the file before you close the laptop.
I saved the photos to a flash drive.
The document had not been saved, and an hour of work was gone.

senses.head: To make it unnecessary for someone to spend time or effort
examples: Taking the express will save you an hour.
One phone call saved us a trip downtown.
You could have saved yourself a lot of trouble by asking first.

entries.русский: копить, откладывать, экономить; спасать, спасти; сохранять, сохранить (файл); избавлять от (хлопот), избавить; экономить (время, силы)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (save money), intransitive (they save for retirement)
